results.title: The set of conjugacy class sizes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a group $G$, $N(G)$ is the set of natural numbers $|\{y \in G : y \text{ is conjugate to } x\}|$ for $x \in G$, that is, the set of sizes of the conjugacy classes of $G$, where an infinite class counts as size $0$.

results.title: Thompson's conjecture on conjugacy class sizes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Write $N(G)$ for the set of sizes of the conjugacy classes of a group $G$. Thompson's conjecture is the statement that for all finite groups $G$ and $H$, if $G$ is simple and non-abelian, $H$ has trivial centre, and $N(G) = N(H)$, then $G$ and $H$ are isomorphic.

results.title: Thompson's conjecture on conjugacy class sizes is true
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all finite groups $G$ and $H$, if $G$ is simple and non-abelian, $H$ has trivial centre, and $G$ and $H$ have the same set of conjugacy class sizes, then $G$ and $H$ are isomorphic.

results.title: Most significant digit
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $b$ and $m$, let $k$ be the base-$b$ logarithm of $m$ rounded down, that is, the largest $k$ with $b^k \le m$ when $b \ge 2$ and $m \ge 1$, and $k = 0$ otherwise. The most significant digit of $m$ in base $b$ is $\lfloor m / b^k \rfloor$. When $b \ge 2$ and $m \ge 1$ this is the leading digit of the base-$b$ expansion of $m$.

results.title: Comma candidate digits
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $b$ and $n$ be natural numbers and let $y$ be a digit with $0 \le y < b$. Put $m = n + b\,(n \bmod b) + y$, where $n \bmod b$ is the remainder of $n$ on division by $b$. Then $y$ is a comma candidate for $n$ in base $b$ if $m > 0$ and the most significant base-$b$ digit of $m$ equals $y$.

results.title: Comma successor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $b$, $n$ and $m$ be natural numbers. Then $m$ is the comma successor of $n$ in base $b$ if there is a comma candidate digit $y < b$ for $n$ in base $b$ such that $m = n + b\,(n \bmod b) + y$ and no digit $y' < y$ is a comma candidate for $n$ in base $b$.

results.title: Comma-terminal numbers
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Numbers that are not comma successors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $b \ge 3$ and $n \ge b^2 - 1$. Then $n$ is not the comma successor in base $b$ of any positive integer if and only if $n = c\, b^i$ for some $i \ge 2$ and some $c$ with $2 \le c \le b - 1$.

results.title: Every number at least the square of the base is a comma-child
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $b \ge 2$ and $n \ge b^2$. Then there are a positive integer $k$ and a comma candidate digit $y$ of $k$ in base $b$ with $n = k + b\,(k \bmod b) + y$, that is, $n$ is a comma-child of $k$.

results.title: The comma-child graph has an infinite path
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every base $b \ge 2$ there is a sequence $a_0, a_1, \dots$ of positive integers such that for every $i$ there is a comma candidate digit $y$ of $a_i$ in base $b$ with $a_{i+1} = a_i + b\,(a_i \bmod b) + y$, that is, each $a_{i+1}$ is a comma-child of $a_i$.

results.title: There is a unique infinite comma-child path from 1 in base 3
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is exactly one sequence $a_0, a_1, \dots$ of natural numbers with $a_0 = 1$ such that for every $i$ there is a comma candidate digit $y$ of $a_i$ in base $3$ with $a_{i+1} = a_i + 3\,(a_i \bmod 3) + y$, that is, each $a_{i+1}$ is a base-3 comma-child of $a_i$.

results.title: Rescaling a representative does not change the projective point
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $V$ be a module over a division ring $K$. For every nonzero scalar $a \in K$ and every nonzero vector $v \in V$, the points of the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(V)$ represented by $a v$ and by $v$ are equal.

results.title: Orthogonality of projective points via representatives
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $m$ a finite set. Let $p, q$ be points of the projective space $\mathbb{P}(K^m)$ and let $\hat p, \hat q \in K^m$ be the fixed nonzero representatives chosen for $p$ and $q$. Then $p$ and $q$ are orthogonal (the dot product of a representative of $p$ with a representative of $q$ vanishes, which does not depend on the representatives) if and only if $\hat p \cdot \hat q = 0$.

results.title: Order of vanishing at a point
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, let $F$ be a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ and let $v \in R^\sigma$. The order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v F \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ of $F$ at $v$ is the order at the origin of the Taylor expansion $F(v + X)$, the polynomial obtained from $F$ by substituting $X_i + v_i$ for each $X_i$: the least total degree of a monomial with nonzero…

results.title: Constant term of the Taylor expansion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, $F$ a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$, and $v \in R^\sigma$. The constant term of the Taylor expansion $F(X + v)$, obtained by substituting $X_i + v_i$ for each $X_i$, is the value $F(v)$.

results.title: Partial derivatives commute with Taylor expansion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, let $F$ be a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_j)_{j \in \sigma}$, let $v \in R^\sigma$ and let $i \in \sigma$. Writing $G(X + v)$ for the polynomial obtained from a polynomial $G$ by substituting $X_j + v_j$ for each $X_j$, we have $\frac{\partial}{\partial X_i}\bigl(F(X + v)\bigr) = \frac{\partial F}{\partial X_i}(X + v)$.

results.title: Vanishing to order at least one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, let $F$ be a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ and let $v \in R^\sigma$. Then the order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v F$ of $F$ at $v$ is at least $1$ if and only if $F(v) = 0$.

results.title: Vanishing to order zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, let $F$ be a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ and let $v \in R^\sigma$. Then the order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v F$ of $F$ at $v$ is $0$ if and only if $F(v) \neq 0$.

results.title: Nonzero constants vanish to order zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring and let $a \in R$ be nonzero. For every point $v \in R^\sigma$, the constant polynomial $a$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ has order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v a = 0$ at $v$.

results.title: Only the zero polynomial vanishes to infinite order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $F$ be a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ and let $v \in R^\sigma$. Then the order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v F \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ of $F$ at $v$ equals $\infty$ if and only if $F = 0$.

results.title: Order of vanishing via first partial derivatives
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be an integral domain of characteristic zero, $F$ a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$, $v \in R^\sigma$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $F$ vanishes to order at least $n + 1$ at $v$ if and only if $F(v) = 0$ and every first partial derivative $\partial F / \partial X_i$ vanishes to order at least $n$ at $v$.

results.title: Vanishing to order at least two via first partial derivatives
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be an integral domain of characteristic zero and let $F$ be a multivariate polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$. For every point $v \in R^\sigma$, the polynomial $F$ vanishes to order at least $2$ at $v$ if and only if $F(v) = 0$ and $\frac{\partial F}{\partial X_i}(v) = 0$ for every $i \in \sigma$.

results.title: Scaling invariance of the order of vanishing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field and let $F$ be a polynomial over $K$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ that is homogeneous of some degree $d$. For every nonzero $c \in K$ and every point $v \in K^\sigma$, the orders of vanishing agree: $\operatorname{ord}_{cv} F = \operatorname{ord}_v F$.

results.title: Multiplicity of a polynomial at a projective point
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $F$ a polynomial over $K$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$. The multiplicity of $F$ at a point $p$ of the projective space $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$ is the order of vanishing of $F$ at the chosen representative $\bar p \in K^\sigma$ of $p$, as a natural number, with the value $\infty$ read as $0$.

results.title: The multiplicity can be computed at any representative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $F$ a homogeneous polynomial over $K$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$. For every nonzero $v \in K^\sigma$, the multiplicity of $F$ at the point $[v]$ of $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$ spanned by $v$ equals the order of vanishing of $F$ at $v$, with the value $\infty$ read as $0$.

results.title: The multiplicity of a nonzero polynomial is its order of vanishing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $F \neq 0$ a polynomial over $K$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$. For every point $p$ of $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$, the multiplicity of $F$ at $p$, viewed in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, equals the order of vanishing of $F$ at the chosen representative $\bar p \in K^\sigma$ of $p$.

results.title: Constants have multiplicity zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field. For every $a \in K$, the constant polynomial $a$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ has multiplicity $0$ at every point $p$ of the projective space $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$. For $a = 0$ this is the junk value of the multiplicity of the zero polynomial.

results.title: Positive multiplicity means vanishing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $F \neq 0$ a polynomial over $K$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$, and $p$ a point of $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$ with chosen representative $\bar p \in K^\sigma$. The multiplicity of $F$ at $p$ is positive if and only if $F(\bar p) = 0$.

results.title: A linear form vanishes to order zero off its hyperplane
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $\sigma$ be a finite set and let $w, v \in K^\sigma$ with $w \cdot v = \sum_{i \in \sigma} w_i v_i \neq 0$. Then the linear form $L = \sum_{i \in \sigma} w_i X_i$ has order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v L = 0$ at $v$.

results.title: A nonzero linear form vanishes to order one on its hyperplane
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $\sigma$ be a finite set and let $w, v \in K^\sigma$ with $w \neq 0$ and $w \cdot v = \sum_{i \in \sigma} w_i v_i = 0$. Then the linear form $L = \sum_{i \in \sigma} w_i X_i$ has order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v L = 1$ at $v$.

results.title: A hyperplane has multiplicity one at its points
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $\sigma$ a finite type and $w \in K^\sigma$ nonzero, and let $p$ be a point of $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$ orthogonal to the point $[w]$ spanned by $w$, that is, $p$ lies on the hyperplane $\sum_i w_i x_i = 0$. Then the linear form $\sum_i w_i X_i$ has multiplicity $1$ at $p$.

results.title: A hyperplane has multiplicity zero off it
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $\sigma$ a finite type and $w \in K^\sigma$ nonzero, and let $p$ be a point of $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$ that is not orthogonal to the point $[w]$ spanned by $w$, that is, $p$ does not lie on the hyperplane $\sum_i w_i x_i = 0$. Then the linear form $\sum_i w_i X_i$ has multiplicity $0$ at $p$.

results.title: Projective morphism to an affine scheme
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $X$ a scheme. A morphism $f : X \to \operatorname{Spec} R$ is projective if there are $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and a closed immersion $i$ of $X$ into $\operatorname{Proj} R[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, the polynomial ring graded by total degree, such that $f$ is $i$ followed by the structure morphism $\operatorname{Proj} R[x_1, \dots, x_n] \to \operatorname{Spec} R$.

results.title: Normal scheme
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A scheme $X$ is normal if for every point $x \in X$ the local ring $\mathcal{O}_{X,x}$ is an integrally closed domain.

results.title: Antisymmetry of the Riemann curvature
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(M, g)$ be a $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold. Its Riemann curvature endomorphism $R$ is antisymmetric in its first two arguments: $R(u, v) w = -R(v, u) w$ for every point $x \in M$ and all tangent vectors $u, v, w \in T_x M$.

results.title: Sectional curvature vanishes on a vector and a multiple of it
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(M, g)$ be a $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold modeled on a finite-dimensional real space (boundary and corners allowed), and let $x \in M$, $u \in T_x M$ and $c \in \mathbb{R}$. Then the sectional curvature at $x$ satisfies $K(u, cu) = 0$: the denominator $\|u\|^2 \|cu\|^2 - \langle u, cu \rangle^2$ of its defining formula vanishes, and the quotient is then $0$ by definition.

results.title: Sectional curvature vanishes on equal vectors
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Scalar curvature
results.caption: Definition

The unit $n$-sphere has scalar curvature $n (n - 1)$.

results.title: Sectional curvature bounded below
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $M$ has sectional curvature at least $k \in \mathbb{R}$ when $K(u, v) \ge k$ for every point $x \in M$ and all linearly independent tangent vectors $u, v \in T_x M$, where $K(u, v)$ is the sectional curvature of the plane spanned by $u$ and $v$.

results.title: Sectional curvature bounded above
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $M$ has sectional curvature at most $k \in \mathbb{R}$ when $K(u, v) \le k$ for every point $x \in M$ and all linearly independent tangent vectors $u, v \in T_x M$, where $K(u, v)$ is the sectional curvature of the plane spanned by $u$ and $v$.

results.title: Ricci curvature bounded below
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $(M, g)$ has Ricci curvature at least $k \in \mathbb{R}$, written $\operatorname{Ric} \ge k g$, when $\operatorname{Ric}_x(v, v) \ge k \|v\|^2$ for every point $x \in M$ and every tangent vector $v \in T_x M$, where $\operatorname{Ric}$ is the Ricci curvature and $\|v\|$ is the norm of $v$ given by $g$.

results.title: Scalar curvature bounded below
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $M$ has scalar curvature at least $k \in \mathbb{R}$ when its scalar curvature at every point $x \in M$ is at least $k$.

results.title: Einstein metric
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A $C^\infty$ Riemannian manifold $(M, g)$ is Einstein when there is a real constant $\lambda$ such that $\operatorname{Ric}_x(v, w) = \lambda \, g_x(v, w)$ for every point $x \in M$ and all tangent vectors $v, w \in T_x M$, where $\operatorname{Ric}$ is the Ricci curvature ([Lang], Einstein manifolds). Ricci-flat is the case $\lambda = 0$.

results.title: Extending a tangent vector of a normed space gives a constant vector field
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a normed space over a nontrivially normed field, viewed as a manifold modelled on itself, so that each tangent space of $F$ is $F$. For every point $x \in F$, tangent vector $u \in T_xF$ and point $y \in F$, the extension of $u$ to a vector field on $F$ (built from the trivialization of the tangent bundle at $x$) has value $u$ at $y$.

results.title: Extensions of tangent vectors of a normed space are differentiable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a normed space over a nontrivially normed field, viewed as a manifold modelled on itself. For every point $x \in F$, tangent vector $u \in T_xF$ and point $y \in F$, the extension of $u$ to a vector field on $F$ (built from the trivialization of the tangent bundle at $x$), viewed as a map from $F$ to its tangent bundle, is differentiable at $y$, not only at the base point $x$.

results.title: Lie brackets of extended tangent vectors of a normed space vanish
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a normed space over a nontrivially normed field, viewed as a manifold modelled on itself. For points $x, x' \in F$ and tangent vectors $a \in T_xF$ and $b \in T_{x'}F$, let $X$ and $Y$ be the extensions of $a$ and $b$ to vector fields on $F$ (built from the trivializations of the tangent bundle at $x$ and at $x'$). Then the Lie bracket $[X, Y]$ vanishes at every point $y \in F$.

results.title: Euclidean space is flat
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space with the Riemannian metric given by its inner product on every tangent space. For every point $x \in F$ and all tangent vectors $u, v, w \in T_xF$, the Riemann curvature endomorphism $R$ of $F$ at $x$ satisfies $R(u, v)w = 0$.

results.title: Euclidean space has zero sectional curvature
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space with the Riemannian metric given by its inner product on every tangent space. For every point $x \in F$ and all tangent vectors $u, v \in T_xF$, the sectional curvature $K(u, v)$ of $F$ at $x$ is $0$.

results.title: Euclidean space is Ricci-flat
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space with the Riemannian metric given by its inner product on every tangent space. For every point $x \in F$ and all tangent vectors $v, w \in T_xF$, the Ricci curvature $\mathrm{Ric}(v, w)$ of $F$ at $x$ is $0$.

results.title: Euclidean space has zero scalar curvature
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space with the Riemannian metric given by its inner product on every tangent space. For every point $x \in F$, the scalar curvature of $F$ at $x$ is $0$.

results.title: Binary digits of a natural number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$ and an integer $i$, the binary digit $n_i \in \{0, 1\}$ of $n$ is the coefficient of $2^i$ in the binary expansion of $n$ when $i \ge 0$, and $n_i = 0$ when $i < 0$.

results.title: Takagi coefficients
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $k$ an integer, and write $n_j$ for the binary digit of $n$ at position $j$ (so $n_j = 0$ for $j < 0$). The Takagi coefficients $\ell_i(n, k)$, for natural numbers $i$, are the natural numbers given by $\ell_0(n, k) = 0$ and, for every natural number $i$, with $s_i = \sum_{j=0}^{i-1} n_{k-j}$, by $\ell_{i+1}(n, k) = s_i$ if $n_{k-i} = 0$ and $\ell_{i+1}(n, k) = i - s_i$ otherwise.

results.title: Takagi function on dyadic presentations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$ and an integer $k$, the Takagi value $\tau(n, k)$ of the dyadic presentation $n / 2^{k+1}$ is the sum of the real series $\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} \ell_{i+1}(n, k) / 2^{i+1}$, where $\ell_i(n, k)$ denotes the $i$-th Takagi coefficient of $n$ and $k$.

results.title: Formula for the binary digits
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every integer $i$, the binary digit $n_i$ of $n$ equals $1$ if $i \ge 0$ and the coefficient of $2^i$ in the binary expansion of $n$ is $1$, and equals $0$ otherwise.

results.title: The Takagi coefficient at index zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every integer $k$, the Takagi coefficient $\ell_0(n, k)$ is $0$.

results.title: Formula for the Takagi coefficients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, every integer $k$ and every natural number $i$, let $s_i = \sum_{j=0}^{i-1} n_{k-j}$, where $n_j$ denotes the binary digit of $n$ at position $j$. Then the Takagi coefficient $\ell_{i+1}(n, k)$ equals $s_i$ if $n_{k-i} = 0$, and equals $i - s_i$ otherwise.

results.title: Series for the Takagi value
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every integer $k$, the Takagi value $\tau(n, k)$ of the dyadic presentation $n / 2^{k+1}$ satisfies $\tau(n, k) = \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} \ell_{i+1}(n, k) / 2^{i+1}$, where $\ell_i(n, k)$ denotes the $i$-th Takagi coefficient of $n$ and $k$.

results.title: Binary digits at negative positions vanish
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every integer $i < 0$, the binary digit $n_i$ of $n$ is $0$.

results.title: The first Takagi coefficient vanishes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every integer $k$, the Takagi coefficient $\ell_1(n, k)$ is $0$.

results.title: Level counts of D-nodes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $i$, let $n_i$ be the binary digit of $n$ at position $i$ (the coefficient of $2^i$ in the binary expansion of $n$). The level count $\lambda_i(n)$ is $n \bmod 2^i$ if $n_i = 0$, and $2^i - (n \bmod 2^i)$ if $n_i = 1$.

results.title: Level count of D-nodes when the binary digit is zero

results.summary: `G` with the taxon placement `ι` is a binary phylogenetic `X`-tree: `G` is a tree, `ι` is injective, the leaves (degree-one vertices) are exactly the taxa, and every other vertex has degree three.

results.title: Taxa on one side of a tree edge
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The taxa on the `a`-side of the edge `{a, b}`: those whose vertex is still joined to `a` once the edge `{a, b}` is deleted.

results.title: Contribution of a split to the neighbor-joining score
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The contribution of one split `{A, Aᶜ}` to the neighbor-joining score of the pair `x, y`: the number of taxa on the far side of the split when `x, y` lie on the same side, and `1` when the split separates them.

results.title: Two sides of a tree edge partition the taxa
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In a tree, the two sides of an edge partition the taxa.

results.title: Splits of two tree edges are compatible
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In a tree, the splits of any two edges are compatible: one side of the first edge lies inside one side of the second.

results.title: Leaf side of a pendant edge
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The leaf side of a pendant edge holds only the leaf's taxon.

results.title: Every edge side of a binary phylogenetic tree is nonempty
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every side of every edge of a binary phylogenetic tree holds a taxon.

results.title: Edge side at an internal vertex as a disjoint union
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At an internal vertex `a` with neighbor `b`, the `a`-side of `{a, b}` is the disjoint union of the far sides of the other two edges at `a`.

results.title: Split decomposition of a tree metric
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The path length between two taxa is half the sum, over the darts (oriented edges) of the tree, of the lengths of the edges whose split separates them.

results.title: Cherry lemma for split systems
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a compatible system of splits with positive weights, containing every trivial split and binary (every side with at least two taxa is the disjoint union of two sides), on at least four taxa, a pair maximizing the total `splitGain` is a side of some split.

results.title: Q-criterion of two singleton clusters
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Q-criterion of two singleton clusters at the start of neighbor joining: `Q({x}, {y}) = (|X| - 2) d x y - ∑_z d x z - ∑_z d y z`.

results.title: The Q-criterion of a split-decomposed dissimilarity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `d x y` is half the total weight of the splits `A e` separating `x` and `y`, then `(|X| - 2) d x y - ∑_z d x z - ∑_z d y z = -∑ e, w e * splitGain (A e) x y`.

results.title: A singleton side is a pendant leaf side
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A side holding a single taxon `z` is the leaf side of `z`'s pendant edge.

results.title: A two-taxon side forms a cherry
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a side of the edge `{a, b}` is the pair `{x, y}`, then `a` is a common neighbor of the leaves `ι x` and `ι y`: they form a cherry.

results.title: On a tree metric, a pair of taxa minimizing the Q-criterion is a cherry
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: (Saitou & Nei 1987; Studier & Keppler 1988; Bryant 2005). Let `d` be the path-length metric of a binary phylogenetic `X`-tree `(G, ι)` with positive edge lengths `w` and at least four taxa. If the distinct taxa `x, y` minimize the Q-criterion over all pairs of distinct singleton clusters at the start of neighbor joining, then `ι x` and `ι y` have a common neighbor.

results.title: The first join of neighbor joining on a tree metric joins a cherry
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On the path-length metric of a binary phylogenetic `X`-tree with positive edge lengths and at least four taxa, any pair of clusters that neighbor joining may join from the initial singletons consists of two taxa with a common neighbor.

results.title: Neighbor joining is exact on tree metrics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let `d` be the path-length metric of a binary phylogenetic `X`-tree `(G, ι)` with positive edge lengths `w`. Then every complete run of neighbor joining (stopped with at most three clusters) forms exactly the splits of the internal edges of the tree: a set of taxa `A` or its complement is a formed cluster if and only if `A` is the set of taxa on the `a`-side of an edge `{a, b}` with both endpoints internal.

results.title: Edwards–Sokal edge factor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Edwards–Sokal factor of an edge `e`: `1 - p` if `e` is closed in `ω`, and `p` times the indicator that `σ` agrees at the endpoints if `e` is open.

results.title: Edwards–Sokal joint weight
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Edwards–Sokal joint weight of a spin configuration `σ` and a bond configuration `ω`: the product of `esEdgeFactor` over the edges of `G`.

results.title: Spin configuration constant on open clusters
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: `σ` is constant on every open edge of `ω`, i.e. on every open cluster.

results.title: Cluster-constant colorings as colorings of clusters
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Colorings constant on open clusters correspond to colorings of the connected components of the open subgraph.

results.title: There are $q^{k(\omega)}$ colorings constant on the open clusters
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: There are `q ^ k(ω)` colorings constant on the open clusters, where `k(ω)` is the number of clusters.

results.title: Edwards–Sokal weight summed over spins is the random-cluster weight
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Spin marginal of the Edwards–Sokal weight: summing over spins gives the random-cluster weight `p^{o(ω)} (1 - p)^{c(ω)} q^{k(ω)}`.

results.title: Edwards–Sokal factor of an arbitrary coordinate and state
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Edwards–Sokal factor of an edge `e` written for an arbitrary pair `(e, b)` with `b` the state of `e`; edges outside `G` get factor `1`.

results.title: Normalizing constant relating the bond sum to the Potts weight
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The normalizing constant `e^{-βJ |E(G)|}` relating the bond marginal to the Potts weight.

results.title: Edwards–Sokal bond sum is a multiple of the Potts weight
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Bond marginal of the Edwards–Sokal weight: with `p = 1 - e^{-βJ}`, summing over bond configurations gives `e^{-βJ |E|}` times the Potts weight of `σ`.

results.title: Edwards–Sokal partition function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Edwards–Sokal partition function: the total joint weight.

results.title: Bond marginal of the Edwards–Sokal measure
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The bond marginal of the normalized Edwards–Sokal measure.

results.title: Spin marginal of the Edwards–Sokal measure

results.title: Edwards–Sokal bond marginal is the random-cluster measure
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: The bond marginal of the Edwards–Sokal measure is the random-cluster measure with parameters `(1 - e^{-βJ}, q)`.

results.title: Edwards–Sokal spin marginal is the Potts measure
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: The spin marginal of the Edwards–Sokal measure is the `q`-state Potts measure at inverse temperature `β` and coupling `J`.
